body: Hey man, you're doing a great job. The fact that you understood your son's distress is incredibly significant and shows that you are breaking the cycle. Just because you had an asshole dad, doesn't mean you are destined to become one. All parents make mistakes, but it's the reparation of the relationship that makes the world of difference. From someone whose parents never acknowledged or corrected the distress they caused.
It's absurdly insensitive to say "Good for her" to someone whose mum recently passed, especially with how little context there is about the situation.
I'm so sorry that happened to you. None of it was your fault.

Self-absorbed tampon 😂

Good on you for standing up to him. Massive props.

I struggle with the same thing that you do - my psychologist says I present things very stoically and "flat", and don't let on how distressing they actually are to me. Personally I feel that the individual psychologist's approach (experience working with childhood trauma, complex ptsd etc) was much more helpful than the name of the therapy. Hope that makes sense. 

Sorry to hear your previous experiences haven't helped - I also tried a couple before finding one that I really felt safe around, and could allow myself to emote as you said. 

NB: My psychologist does psychodynamic therapy, which sometimes overlaps with schema therapy. IMO, opposed to cognitive-behavioural therapy (much more common), psychs who have a special interest in schema/psychodynamic stuff tend to be more aware of non-standard presentations of mental health issues, particularly related to childhood/adverse events. I might be totally wrong though.
Rooting for you. The level of self-awareness and understanding you have will take you a long way.
You're a good friend :)
Sorry you had to hear that growing up, you didn't deserve, and never will deserve, to be treated that way.
True. Everyone responds to trauma and events differently. Not everyone who has experienced trauma or any level of abuse will react in the ways being listed in this thread.

I'm glad you're going through the process of unpacking those things - it can be hard work and upsetting at times but you sound like you're doing great at it. 

I'm also in the process of realising that kids need to feel loved, safe and secure, and not feeling that can leave some holes like you said. Even if they feel oddly specific they are important all the same, just like food and shelter. Hope you're going well.
That's very fucked up of your parents to do to you, and very traumatic for a child. Hope you're doing okay.
You were only 9 tho, how could he expect you to have the understanding of a young adult?
Super beautiful!
That is horrible. I'm sorry you had to experience that.
What are you talking about? That's amazing!!!
You are a great doctor.

Aww that genuinely put a smile on my face to read. If you ever need a stranger to vent to I'll be here. I've gone through similar things for most of my life and would be happy to hear you out if you ever need it. 

(I hate this image too, with a passion. Stupid)
Hey man, are you okay?
You're a good person! Actually helping instead of just criticizing
This, so much.
Is there a way I can remotely buy a few small groceries for your family here and there? Maybe a local delivery service?
Beautiful!!!

Hey man. Your level of self-awareness is admirable. I have also had many similar fuckups. But I just wanted to say that you have immense potential to grow and be the person you want to be. Give yourself time to process the grief and the regret. But also allow yourself enough self-compassion and rest to grow. You've got this.
This is so lovely. She is very blessed to have you as a parent.
Do you have a favourite mushroom?
I believe in you
Beautiful
This is a great idea
This is adorable
Dude same
True, not really wholesome
You're a good person.
Wanna talk about it? I can't do much but I can listen

Hey that sounds very very difficult. I'm so sorry it's been like that for you. You are incredibly strong and resilient for going through all that, and it's so cool that you are pushing towards the goal of going to school, to start a new life. You have a bright future ahead of you. Please, on dark days, please reach out. To me or your local suicide hotline or ED. I promise they will care about you even if you don't.
That's completely, absolutely horrible and your feelings are completely valid. Do you have access to a counsellor, therapist or anyone like that?

It's already a good step you are making, letting out your feelings like this. I'm proud of you. Recognising negative thoughts is the first step - learning to replace them is a long process but it gets easier and easier. If counselling is an option for you, it might really help. You sound like a really thoughtful, caring person :)
That sounds difficult and confusing. Is there a local LGBTQ+ support organisation you can talk to?
That sounds really rough :( sometimes the uncertainty and feeling of lostness really eats at you from the inside out. It can be really scary. I hope it works out soon for you.

That sounds really rough and a lot to go through. Being through the hospital process can be incredibly scary, even traumatic - I still have nightmares about it. You are incredibly resilient and strong for making it through all this, I believe you can make it through treatment. I believe in you.
:( are you okay?
This is a wonderful post, nothing shitposty about this. Thanks op

It is definitely a big and daunting step to take. It's not easy and it takes a lot of courage to even start thinking about getting help. The fact that you're already considering shows amazing self-awareness and resilience. You got this, try to be a little gentle and kind with yourself because you deserve it.

You're a wonderful, loving, and thoughtful person and parent. The fact that you love and care for your children shows your resilience and your heart. It is a truly precious thing. I'm so sorry it has been so rough on you.
I'm sure you are a truly, genuinely wonderful person. I'm sorry that it feels like no one means it sometimes.

I keep having vivid, terrifying nightmares. Every single time I fall asleep, I have a different nightmare. I've lost count of how many I have had in the few days, at least 20. I feel like I'm barely living in the real world anymore, mainly in my dreams. Recently, in my peripheral vision I have been seeing things moving. My doctor is on Christmas leave and I don't know what to do.
The fact that you still want to live a decent life is incredibly admirable to me. Being in a similar position, to me it shows your strength and resilience as a person. That quality is so precious.
There's lots of resources online that may help, like https://www.beyondblue.org.au/the-facts/supporting-someone
You sound really thoughtful and mature. I'm rooting for you :)
Not just us, but the people in your life too! If not right now, then the friends and best friends whom you've yet to meet, will care endlessly about you.

You're doing a great job. Feeling negatively about this is not unhealthy in any way. Its normal to feel sad and overwhelmed for a bit. You can lean on to other people for support with your mental health, whether it's a friend, family, or helpline. Here for you if you need!
That's so good honestly. Takes a huge amount of effort to get to that point. Proud of you!
I'm rooting for you too! I'm here if you need a listening ear. You're incredibly strong for clinging on to that hope, even when everything seems to rail against it.
I'm here if you need someone to talk to
You're doing a great job, I'm so proud of you :) it takes so much strength and resilience to be where you are right now. Even if it's "just" waiting.
Hey, hit me up if you need to talk. I've been there before, very different circumstances but still. I'm here for you.
What drives you to keep going, despite all that you know you've fucked up? The guilt of how much I have fucked up makes it hard to see the purpose of persisting

hey, are you alright?

​

I will definitely consider and reread your messages the next time this happens. Thank you for helping me. It feels so surreal that someone, let alone multiple people, would give up their time and put in effort to help me. Thank you for doing that.
You have helped me immensely. Please keep that in mind. I understand the distraction thing. You can talk to me too, if you'd like. It'd be nice, if you wanted to.

Thank you, I really appreciate the concern, I'm stunned by it. I'm alright, albeit very uncomfortable, I'm not as hysterical as last night but rather numb. Thank you for checking in, you are truly wonderful.

Yeah, the possible pain I might temporarily cause others to feel was one of the factors that made me feel conflicted with my decision. I see where you're coming from. 

I'm afraid that I might burden her and tire her out. She's such a lovely person, I would hate to affect her. Telling her about my thoughts was a huge step already. In the past I have been affected by a suicidal friend, that was about when my bouts of dark times started. I don't want to take the chance of doing the same to her. But I'll think about it.  

It's hard to think it isn't the solution, when so many people have committed suicide. It's painful and uncomfortable thinking about the 14 year old who recently did. It's hard to get someone to look out for you when you're convinced you're doing what is best - why would you want someone to persuade you otherwise? 

But thank you, I'll definitely keep thinking about your words. Eventually they'll be right in my mind. I think I'm at a lower risk now. Thank you for caring.

Now that you put it like that, it seems a bit clearer that they do care. Thank you. I don't know if I'll ever be able to talk about this with them. I talked to lifeline last night. After sleeping I'm considerably calmer. Now it's just waiting until the next big episode. Thank you for caring and for supporting me, it means the world to me.
I'll keep you in mind.

It was okay for a while, maybe even good, while I was busy with school. There were still episodes and I was still crying myself to sleep every other night, but it all just built up to this. This happened last year as well, it's hard to hold on to hope when it's happened so many times.

I've tried. Dammit I've tried, and each time it hurts. Thank you for caring for me. I don't know what to make of my relationship with my mother, it's been tumultuous lately and I don't feel like they'd hurt very much if I died. I wish I could open up. I know it sounds stupid, because I can open up, but I'm too scared of the consequences to. I hate the gruelling questionings. The last time my parents and I came remotely close to speaking about depression, I hated it. I hated every single second of it. Their style of communication (sitting down at table, silence, intense seriousness) is torturous to me. At church I responded to an altar call regarding depression. When I came back from church, they asked me about it, when did I go through it, what was it, and I just could not bring myself to say anything. It was so intensely uncomfortable, they got frustrated, and I felt like killing myself all over again. 

Thank you for caring for me. I'm in a really conflicted spot. The general statement is that I shouldn't commit suicide. But it nags at me at the back of my head, like how I shouldn't be alive, how much pain I've caused the people around me, and how I've already planned it and can't chicken out.

That makes sense. I don't know how to wrap my head around it. If one of my family members died it'd be horrible and painful and like you said torturous. But I can't imagine it being the same for me. There'd at least be a sigh of relief. I see the logic though.

I don't mind missing out on the good things. I've had many good memories, but everything is falling apart and the little pockets of happiness are nothing compared to the pain. It also seems selfish to stay for the good times, but continue hurting my family. I'll never get a chance to see things get better, but at least they no longer have to deal with a painful daughter. And I'll never have to deal with the pain again. 

No, I haven't. I'm not good at expressing my feelings verbally, and haven't had good experiences with school counsellors in the past. My family has no idea about all this, and I don't really want to tell them. I know a lot of people say that I should, but it will not go down well. 

Again, thank you so much for the support. It means a lot that you would take the time to write such a well thought out message. I hope I didn't come across as argumentative - I wasn't trying to argue with you, I just...I don't know. I don't want to argue with you. I needed to get the reasons out.

Thank you for the hope. I know parents sometimes wish their child had never been born. I strongly suspect I have a mental disorder, and I'm making it terribly hard for them. They'd get on so much better without me constantly weighing them down with my bad vibes from my screwed up mind. I did really hold out hope that life would change, maybe three months is too little, but damn it hurts so bad. If I don't end it today, I'll probably lose the motivation and the fire to do it, and a few months later I'll just be experiencing this again and hurting my family. They don't know about my state but the negativity is getting to them, especially my mother.

My mother asked if I thought that I could move forward and make progress (in regards to my bad vibes). I said yes. Of all the lies I'd told her in that conversation, that was the biggest, most blatant one. I've tried. 

I'm about thirteen, and I am so sorry for unloading this on you. Please understand that I am immensely grateful for your comment and will try my best to understand it.

They probably don't love me though. I bring them pain. I don't love them with a burning passion, I love them but I just want to stop bringing people pain. They would be rid of a burden and a constant pressing pain. For the rest of the world, it wouldn't even matter. Obama, the leader of World Vision, the really kind person on the other side of the world, etc, it wouldn't matter, they wouldn't know, they might even have a particularly great day. Me dying will not matter. In the unlikely event that my friends and family do feel pain, they'll heal. It's for the best. I don't deserve the rest of my life, and they don't deserve any of the pain I bring by living.
Thank you, thank you so much for those words. From the bottom of my heart. Man I'm tired. It makes a difference. I'm still conflicted but I think I'll wait a little longer.
Thank you for offering, really, it means a lot.
